trust_decision.summary: The UDP receive worker trusts the stream's datagram stride (settings->blksize, which a remote client can set through the 'len' test parameter) to advance its per-datagram loop. At the pinned commit, a dgram_sz<=0 guard in iperf_udp_recv and a UDP blksize range check in iperf_get_parameters already enforce this.

landing_point.why: The summary names the UDP receive worker loop. This while loop advances by dgram_sz, and dgram_sz comes from blksize at src/iperf_udp.c:90 and :95.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: unknown: the published fix commit contains no source change, so there is no route the fix leaves open to argue about

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: UDP blksize 0 on the client means 'derive from MSS', and gso_dg_size 0 falls back to DEFAULT_UDP_BLKSIZE. A fix that rejects every zero size at option parsing would break this.

O7_producer.where: src/iperf_api.c:2654-2660 (iperf_get_parameters stores the client 'len' into settings->blksize; it is validated later at src/iperf_api.c:2810-2815)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The GRO branch takes stride from blksize and length from gro_bf_size, and gro_bf_size from the client is only checked for being >= 0 (src/iperf_api.c:2709-2715). A stride/length sibling would fit here.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The GRO/GSO code is newly added, and its size parameters are accepted from the client with sign checks only.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: gso_dg_size and gso_bf_size from the client are stored with only a sign check, and the derivation only guards the >0 case. Removing the stride guard from the send loop (src/iperf_udp.c:270) would make a realistic sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The send loop at src/iperf_udp.c:285 has the same shape as the receive loop, and a maintainer could have guarded only one of the two.

O9_family: CWE-835 loop with unreachable exit (zero/invalid datagram stride in the UDP receive loop)

O10_build.project_tests: src/t_*.c unit tests via 'make check' (e.g. t_units, t_uuid, t_api, t_timer); I found none that cover the UDP receive loop

j.j_sites_touched: Makefile.in, aclocal.m4, config/*, configure, examples/Makefile.in, src/Makefile.in (no C source)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a dgram_sz<=0 early return in iperf_udp_recv and nothing else. This guard already exists at src/iperf_udp.c:107-110 at the pinned commit.

out_of_scope_notes: The same release also fixes a server UAF (CVE-2026-101283) and an iperf_auth.c heap overflow (CVE-2026-101276) per RELNOTES.md:9-16; I did not pursue either.
unverified: The advisory's fix_commits (926bd90) is an autotools regen ('Regen.'): it changes Makefile.in, aclocal.m4, config/*, configure, examples/Makefile.in and src/Makefile.in, with no C source (fix.diff:5-4010). It does not fix the loop.

The loop guards are already present at the pinned commit (src/iperf_udp.c:107-110; src/iperf_api.c:2810-2815), and RELNOTES.md:18-19 already credits the CVE fix. The real fix is probably the merged branch 'ip3-419_loop' (f990182), an ancestor of the pin. I did not verify this; I could not run git.
Because of this, the pinned tree is NOT vulnerable to the advisory. A correct pin would be the parent of the ip3-419_loop fix commits.
The O8 analysis of the true pre-fix tree was not done. Whether 'len' 0 from the client reached iperf_udp_recv before the fix is unknown.
